A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MOCOBO work, with complete main text, figures, tables, Appendices A.1–A.10, and checklist. Full-text comparison and inspection of rendered pages and matching graphics support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original optimization experiments on peptide design, molecule design, rover navigation, and image tone mapping, plus in vitro peptide assays and appendix ablation and runtime results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original optimization experiments, in vitro MIC measurements, and appendix ablation and runtime results.

M1.justification: The coverage objective, ECI acquisition, greedy covering-set approximation, coordinated trust regions, and batch approximation remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same peptide, molecule, rover, and tone-mapping tasks, including template-free/constrained peptides, both benchmark images, and the appendix scenario with highly conflicting rover objectives.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain CluSO, TuRBO/LOL-BO, ROBOT, MORBO, random sampling, and T individually optimized solutions. Their participation and adaptations described in Section 4 are unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, covering-set sizes, acquisition batch size, initialization data, surrogate configurations, training procedures, and assay settings remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A.1 and A.7–A.8.

E4.justification: The oracle-partition ablation in Section 4.3, highly conflicting-objectives study in Appendix A.2.2, runtime analysis in A.2.3, and qualitative covering-set examples are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 optimization replications with standard errors, 10 runtime measurements with standard errors in Table A.3, and three biological replicates for the antibacterial assays.

E6.justification: Reported curves, MIC measurements, molecular scores, and runtime values are unchanged. For example, Appendix A.2.2 retains average coverage scores of 2.932 for MOCOBO and 12.899 for T individually optimized solutions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, acquisition equations, NP-hardness result, approximation guarantee, and associated proofs in Appendices A.9–A.10 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same scientific contributions and claims about coverage optimization, comparative performance, and antimicrobial discovery. The added abstract sentence concerns code access.

C2.justification: Interpretations of peptide specialization, misleading image-quality metrics, and conflicting objectives remain unchanged, as do the limitations concerning selection of K and the future-work discussion in Appendix A.4.

D1.justification: v3 replaces placeholder links and post-acceptance release promises with the nataliemaus/mocobo repository address in the abstract, Section 4, Appendix A.7, and checklist. Section 4 now specifically describes code for MOCOBO results on all tasks. Implementation details are unchanged; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to Bayesian optimization, gradient-based coverage methods, and CluSO.

P1.justification: Localized edits add or revise code-availability statements and update the arXiv version/date stamp. The narrative, terminology, section order, and remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: The code-access edits cause small positional and page-break shifts, including moving Figure 1 downward on page 2. Graphics, table structures, captions, axes, and legends remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 leaves code access as placeholders and promises release after acceptance; v3 supplies a specific repository address and updates the availability statements throughout the paper. This provides a limited improvement in reproducibility documentation. Scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, and the PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or usability.
